title.es: Leer el guion de una escena

es: Leer un guion breve y distinguir diálogo, acotaciones y subtexto, explicando lo que un personaje quiere decir en realidad.

teaching.en: In a typical script, the dialogue shows what each character says aloud, while short notes in brackets describe what that character does.
teaching.es: En un guion típico, el diálogo muestra lo que cada personaje dice en voz alta, mientras que breves notas entre paréntesis describen lo que hace.
teaching.explanationEs: Script = guion; character = personaje; el diálogo se pronuncia y lo demás se lee.
segments: In a typical script, the dialogue shows what each character says
aloud, while short notes in brackets describe what that character does.
teaching.audioText: In a typical script, the dialogue shows what each character says aloud, while short notes in brackets describe what that character does.

teaching.en: A stage direction such as (She looks away and begins to whisper.) tells the actor how to move or speak, but the audience never hears it read aloud.
teaching.es: Una acotación como (Ella mira hacia otro lado y empieza a susurrar.) le dice al actor cómo moverse o hablar, pero el público nunca la oye leída.
teaching.explanationEs: Stage direction = acotación; whisper = susurrar. Va entre paréntesis y en presente.
segments: A stage direction such as (She looks away and begins to whisper.) tells the
actor how to move or speak, but the audience never hears it read aloud.
teaching.audioText: A stage direction such as (She looks away and begins to whisper.) tells the actor how to move or speak, but the audience never hears it read aloud.

teaching.en: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud in the scene, even though the audience may doubt that it is true.
teaching.es: La línea «Estoy bien» es diálogo, porque el personaje la dice en voz alta en la escena, aunque el público dude de que sea verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Line = cada frase que dice un personaje; scene = escena.
segments: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud
in the scene, even though the audience may doubt that it is true.
teaching.audioText: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud in the scene, even though the audience may doubt that it is true.

teaching.en: The subtext is what a character tries to hide: she says she is fine, but what she really means is that she wants somebody to stay.
teaching.es: El subtexto es lo que un personaje intenta ocultar: dice que está bien, pero lo que realmente quiere decir es que quiere que alguien se quede.
teaching.explanationEs: Subtext = subtexto; hide = ocultar; mean = querer decir. Fórmula: says … but means …
segments: The subtext is what a character tries to hide: she says she is
fine, but what she really means is that she wants somebody to stay.
teaching.audioText: The subtext is what a character tries to hide: she says she is fine, but what she really means is that she wants somebody to stay.

teaching.en: A long pause before an answer can imply that the speaker is choosing words carefully, and attentive viewers learn to read between the lines.
teaching.es: Una pausa larga antes de una respuesta puede dar a entender que quien habla elige con cuidado sus palabras, y los espectadores atentos aprenden a leer entre líneas.
teaching.explanationEs: Pause = pausa; imply = insinuar; read between the lines = captar lo que no se dice.
segments: A long pause before an answer can imply that the speaker is
choosing words carefully, and attentive viewers learn to read between the lines.
teaching.audioText: A long pause before an answer can imply that the speaker is choosing words carefully, and attentive viewers learn to read between the lines.

teaching.en: In this scene the character asks about the weather because she wants to avoid the real topic, and the audience understands without being told.
teaching.es: En esta escena el personaje pregunta por el tiempo porque quiere evitar el tema real, y el público lo entiende sin que nadie se lo diga.
teaching.explanationEs: Evitar el tema real también es subtexto: lo importante no se dice.
segments: In this scene the character asks about the weather because she wants
to avoid the real topic, and the audience understands without being told.
teaching.audioText: In this scene the character asks about the weather because she wants to avoid the real topic, and the audience understands without being told.

prompt.es: Clasifica la línea del texto: ¿diálogo, acotación o subtexto?

choices.text: A stage direction: it describes what Sara does and how she speaks.
A line of dialogue: Sara says it aloud to the other character.
Subtext: it shows what Sara feels but does not say.

feedback.es: Va entre paréntesis y describe el gesto y el tono de Sara: es una acotación, nadie la pronuncia.

hint.es: Fíjate en el paréntesis y en los verbos que describen lo que hace.

origin.text: (Sara looks at the door and begins to whisper.)

prompt.es: Completa: «Ese significado oculto se llama subtexto.»

feedback.es: El subtexto es el significado escondido debajo de las palabras, que el personaje no pronuncia.

hint.es: Es el significado que queda debajo de las palabras.

origin.text: In the script, Tom says 'Fine, go without me', but the long pause before it shows that he is hurt. That hidden meaning is called the ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ella dice que está bien, pero quiere que él se quede.»

answer.text: She says she is fine but she means she wants him to stay

feedback.es: Says … but means … contrapone lo que se pronuncia con el subtexto: she wants him to stay.

hint.es: Empieza por She says y usa but para contrastar.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada línea del guion con su tipo.

pairs: He is angry, but he hides it.

feedback.es: Lo que se hace y cómo se dice va entre paréntesis (acotación), lo que se pronuncia es diálogo y lo que se oculta es subtexto.

pairs: He is angry, but he hides it.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena narrada y elige qué sugiere que la hija oculta algo.

choices.text: She asks her father to help her with the suitcase.
She avoids the question by changing the subject.
She says she is too excited to sleep before the trip.

feedback.es: La hija responde con el tiempo y el cansancio en lugar de hablar de la maleta: evita la pregunta, y eso es subtexto.

origin.audio: In the scene, a father asks his daughter whether she has packed for the trip. She answers that everything is fine, then asks what the weather will be like in the north, then says that she is tired. She never answers the question about her suitcase, and at the end she whispers that she will do it tomorrow. The audience begins to suspect that she does not want to go at all.

prompt.es: Explica el subtexto en una frase con «says … but means …».

answer.text: Tom says it is great, but he means it is bad.
accepted: Tom says it is great, but he means it is bad.
Tom says the food is great, but he means he dislikes it.
Tom says the food is great, but he means it is not good.

feedback.es: El gesto contradice la frase: Tom deja la comida en el plato, así que quiere decir que no le gusta.

origin.text: TOM: The food is great. (He leaves the food on his plate.)

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué hace Tom al final.

choices.text: He asks her to tell him about the project at once.
He goes to bed before she finishes eating.
He keeps her dinner warm without saying anything more.

feedback.es: Tom dice que lo entiende y guarda la cena en el horno: un gesto en lugar de más preguntas.

origin.audio: In the scene, Sara comes home late and finds Tom still awake at the kitchen table. He asks whether the meeting went well. She answers that it was fine and that she is not hungry. After a long pause she says that the manager mentioned a new project, and that she would rather not talk about it tonight. Tom says that he understands, but he quietly puts her dinner in the oven.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere la pausa larga de Sara.

choices.text: That the meeting was not as fine as she says.
That she is thinking about what to cook for dinner.
That she has not understood Tom's question.

feedback.es: La pausa contradice su «it was fine»: da a entender que algo del proyecto la preocupa.

origin.audio: In the scene, Sara comes home late and finds Tom still awake at the kitchen table. He asks whether the meeting went well. She answers that it was fine and that she is not hungry. After a long pause she says that the manager mentioned a new project, and that she would rather not talk about it tonight. Tom says that he understands, but he quietly puts her dinner in the oven.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quien se fija en los gestos sabe leer entre líneas.»

feedback.es: Read between the lines es captar lo que los personajes sugieren sin decirlo.

origin.text: The script says '(He looks at his watch.)', but Tom answers: 'No, stay, it is a great party.' A reader who notices the difference learns to read between the ___.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué función cumple la acotación «after a pause»?

choices.text: It gives the actor a sentence to say aloud.
It hints that Sara is not being completely honest.
It tells the director where to place the camera.

feedback.es: La acotación describe una pausa antes de hablar: sugiere duda y contradice el «Really» de la primera línea.

origin.text:
SARA: (putting the keys on the table) It is a lovely apartment, Tom. Really.
TOM: You do not have to be polite.
SARA: (after a pause) I only said that the street is a little noisy.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué da a entender Sara con su última línea?

choices.text: That she is too busy to go to the party and says so openly.
That she is angry with Tom because he asked her twice.
That she does not really want to go, although she avoids saying so.

feedback.es: Sus respuestas evasivas y la acotación «does not look up» revelan que no quiere ir, aunque no lo diga.

origin.text:
TOM: Are you coming to the party on Friday?
SARA: I have a lot of work.
TOM: It is only one night.
SARA: Maybe. (She does not look up.)

prompt.es: Completa: «Una pausa larga puede dar a entender que se eligen bien las palabras.»

feedback.es: Imply significa dar a entender algo sin decirlo de forma directa: la pausa insinúa cuidado al hablar.

origin.text: Even when a character says very little, silence carries meaning. A long pause can ___ that the speaker is choosing every word with great care.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La acotación describe lo que se ve, no lo que se dice.»

answer.text: A stage direction describes what we see not what people say

feedback.es: What we see y what people say contraponen la acotación (lo visible) al diálogo (lo que se pronuncia).
